docs.title: Defining Confluent Cloud Resources with Terraform
docs.text:
Version

Last updated: 2026-11-24

This section presents the steps to deploy the Confluent Cloud components for Streamhouse using Terraform.

Terraform is organized under the IaC/ directory as independent root modules (separate local state), each file-per-concern:

Module Wrapper script Purpose When IaC/ccloud none (run terraform directly) Core Confluent Cloud: environment, Kafka cluster, Flink compute pools, Schema Registry API key, service accounts, Kafka/Flink API keys, topics. Needs no AWS credentials. Always, first IaC/rtce none (run terraform directly) Real-Time Context Engine / Lightning Query API: Global API key and registration of fct_c360_profile and fct_crm_summary as RTCE topics. After dbt run IaC/AWS scripts/tf_aws.sh PostgreSQL RDS 17 (CDC-ready), security group, KMS, Secrets Manager secret. Opt-in (cost) IaC/connector scripts/tf_connector.sh Managed Debezium PostgreSQL CDC source connector. Reads IaC/ccloud state and the RDS secret. Opt-in (cost) IaC/EC2 scripts/tf_ec2.sh EC2 app host for the backend and frontend containers. Reads IaC/AWS state. Opt-in

This split lets the core Confluent Cloud stack run locally with no AWS credentials. AWS, the managed connector and the app host are opt-in cost paths. For a CDC path with no AWS at all, see Local CDC.

Apply order: IaC/ccloud → dbt run → IaC/rtce. Add IaC/AWS → IaC/connector for the managed CDC path, and IaC/EC2 to host the apps.

The figure below illustrates what the Terraform in IaC/ccloud/ deploys. We start from an existing Organization, a user or service account with the Org Admin role, and a Confluent Cloud Resource API key and secret.

docs.title: What IaC/ccloud creates
docs.text:
File Resources provider.tf Requires only the confluentinc/confluent provider (~> 2.88.0). env.tf Environment ${prefix}-env with the ESSENTIALS stream governance package. This auto-provisions Schema Registry. kafka.tf Standard, single-zone Kafka cluster ${prefix}-kafka. Service account ${prefix}-kafka-mgr with CloudClusterAdmin on the cluster, and its Kafka API key. flink.tf Three Flink compute pools: ${prefix}-flink-pool (c360), ${prefix}-crm-flink-pool (crm) and ${prefix}-snapshot-q-pool (snapshot queries). Service account ${prefix}-flink-runner with EnvironmentAdmin and Assigner (on itself), and the environment/region-scoped Flink API key. Optional Cost API billing role binding. No Flink statements: dbt deploys them. schema_registry.tf Looks up the environment's Schema Registry and creates its API key, owned by the existing cc_sa_env_mgr service account (read in data.tf). topics.tf Topic agent_conversations (chat request/response events) and the Kafka Connect storage topics my_connect_configs, my_connect_offsets and my_connect_status (compacted). variables.tf Inputs. See below. outputs.tf Values consumed by scripts/set_env_from_tf.sh to build the application environment.

The compute pool max_cfu is set by flink_max_cfu (c360) and flink_crm_max_cfu (crm and snapshot pools, default 50 each).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: environment_id, env_display_name, cc_region, cloud_provider, kafka_id, kafka_name, kafka_bootstrap_endpoint, kafka_rest_endpoint, kafka_api_key_id / _secret, sa_id, sa_name, flink_compute_pool_id, flink_crm_compute_pool_id, flink_sn_compute_pool_id, flink_runner_sa_id, flink_api_key_id / _secret, schema_registry_id, schema_registry_rest_endpoint, schema_registry_api_key_id / _secret, plus agent_conversations_topic and debezium_topics.

docs.title: What IaC/rtce creates
docs.text:
The module reads the environment and cluster ids from ../ccloud/terraform.tfstate through terraform_remote_state (same pattern as IaC/connector). Data sources expose the cluster rbac_crn and the Schema Registry resource_name for the role bindings.

  • rtce.tf:
    • service account ${prefix}-rtce-lightning;
    • role bindings: CloudClusterAdmin on the Kafka cluster and ResourceOwner on all Schema Registry subjects;
    • the Global API key (managed_resource kind Global);
    • confluent_rtce_topic.fct_c360_profile and confluent_rtce_topic.fct_crm_summary, which register those existing topics with RTCE so the Lightning Query API serves them. Add more confluent_rtce_topic resources to expose other fact or dimension tables.
  • outputs.tf: rtce_lightning_sa_id, rtce_lightning_api_key_id / _secret (used for CONFLUENT_GLOBAL_KEY / CONFLUENT_GLOBAL_SECRET), rtce_c360_profile_topic_name, rtce_crm_summary_topic_name.

docs.title: Pre-requisites
docs.text:
• git cli
  • Terraform cli (the modules declare required_version >= 1.16.3)
  • Clone this repository: 
    git clone https://github.com/jbcodeforce/streamhouse_c360_demo.git
cd streamhouse_c360_demo

docs.title: Get Confluent Cloud environment information
docs.text:
• Log in to the Confluent Console.

  • Get your user identifier if you are an organization admin, or ask your Organization administrator for a service account that has the Org Admin role. A user id starts with u-, a service account id with sa-. This id is the cc_sa_env_mgr value below.

    A service account is recommended.

    Verify that this service account has the Org Admin role binding:

    * Get the API key and secret for Cloud resource management, or create a new one:

    * Export the key and secret as environment variables in a fresh terminal session. They are the only Confluent Cloud credentials you provide. Everything else (ids, Kafka, Flink and Schema Registry keys) comes from the Terraform outputs: 

    export CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY=PQ...
export CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_SECRET=cflt....
    * In IaC/ccloud/, copy terraform.tfvars.example to terraform.tfvars and fill in the values: 
    cp IaC/ccloud/terraform.tfvars.example IaC/ccloud/terraform.tfvars

    Variable Default Description cc_sa_env_mgr required Existing service account (sa-...) that owns the Schema Registry API key. prefix j9r-jtbd1 Prefix for all resource names. cloud_provider AWS Cloud of the Kafka cluster and Flink pools. aws_region_primary us-west-2 Region of the Kafka cluster and Flink pools. flink_max_cfu / flink_crm_max_cfu 50 / 50 Max CFUs per compute pool. cost_api_principal_id null Principal (sa-... / u-...) behind CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY. When set, it gets cost_api_billing_role (default OrganizationAdmin) so the backend Cost API can read billing data. Leave it unset if that principal is already Org Admin. agent_conversations_topic / _partitions agent_conversations / 6 Chat history topic.

    The example file contains cost_api_principal_id = with no value. Set a value or comment the line out before running Terraform.

    Do NOT commit terraform.tfvars. It is gitignored in this repo.

docs.title: Perform the deployment
docs.text:
Run the commands below from the IaC/ccloud folder:

cd IaC/ccloud

  • Initialize Terraform: 

    terraform init

  • Run the plan to assess what will be created: 

    terraform plan

  • Deploy the resources: 

    terraform apply

    Some resources may take time to create.

  • The outputs are printed at the end. You can retrieve them at any time with: 

    terraform output

  • Validate in the Confluent Console that the resources are created:

  • Write the API keys and ids into apps/backend/.env: 

    cd ../..   # repo root
./scripts/set_env_from_tf.sh

    This reads the outputs of IaC/ccloud and updates apps/backend/.env, created from .env.example if missing. The variables written are:

    Source Variables IaC/ccloud ENVIRONMENT_ID, FLINK_ENV_ID, CLOUD_REGION, CLOUD_PROVIDER, KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID, KAFKA_CLUSTER_NAME, KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, KAFKA_API_KEY / _SECRET IaC/ccloud (Flink) FLINK_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, FLINK_CRM_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, FLINK_SNAPSHOT_COMPUTE_POOL_ID, FLINK_API_KEY / _SECRET, FLINK_REST_ENDPOINT, FLINK_CATALOG (environment display name), FLINK_DATABASE (Kafka cluster name) IaC/ccloud (Schema Registry) SCHEMA_REGISTRY_URL, SCHEMA_REGISTRY_API_KEY / _SECRET IaC/rtce CONFLUENT_GLOBAL_KEY / _SECRET. Empty until that stack is applied (see below). IaC/AWS (if applied) DATABASE_URL, built from the RDS outputs and the password in Secrets Manager. Needs the AWS CLI and jq. Otherwise the existing database settings are kept.

    Run source scripts/set_env_from_tf.sh instead to also export the variables into your current shell.

docs.title: dbt
docs.text:
dbt run can be applied in a CI/CD process with a SHA guard to avoid redeploying materialized tables that were not modified. The dbt project is in pipelines/. Set the environment variables first:

set -a
source apps/backend/.env
set +a

The current lineage is presented by running:

cd pipelines
dbt docs generate
dbt docs serve

The green topics are created by applications or the CDC connector.

The command below deploys to the target environment:

dbt run --select +c360.facts.fct_c360_profile

This creates all the topics in the Kafka cluster:

Topics created by dbt

docs.title: Enable the Real-Time Context Engine (RTCE / Lightning Query API)
docs.text:
The analytics "Customer lookup via RTCE" section queries fct_c360_profile through Confluent's Lightning Query API, a current-state point-lookup serving layer. Enabling it is a separate stack (IaC/rtce) because it must run after the tables exist.

Order of operations:

  1. IaC/ccloud applied (previous sections): environment and Kafka cluster.
  2. dbt run: creates the fct_c360_profile and fct_crm_summary upsert/compacted topics.
  3. IaC/rtce applied: Global key, and registration of the topics with RTCE.

Prerequisites:

  • The Real-Time Context Engine / Lightning Query API Early Access feature must be enabled for your Confluent organization. Without it the Lightning API reports the org as not found (HTTP 400) regardless of this stack.
  • An OrganizationAdmin Cloud API key for the Terraform provider. Creating a service account, a Global API key and an RTCE topic are org-level operations, and a resource-scoped key returns 401. Provide it as CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY / CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_SECRET, or as confluent_cloud_api_key / confluent_cloud_api_secret in terraform.tfvars.
  • The topics named by profile_topic (fct_c360_profile) and crm_summary_topic (fct_crm_summary) already exist (step 2 done).
  • The IaC/ccloud state at core_state_path (default ../ccloud/terraform.tfstate).

Deploy:

cd IaC/rtce
cp terraform.tfvars.example terraform.tfvars   # set prefix / cloud / region to match IaC/ccloud
terraform init
terraform apply

The same CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY / CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_SECRET variables are used. There is no wrapper script for this module.

This creates a dedicated service account, grants it CloudClusterAdmin on the cluster and ResourceOwner on the Schema Registry subjects, creates the Global API key, and registers the two topics with RTCE through confluent_rtce_topic.

Wire the key into the backend:

cd ../..                      # repo root
./scripts/set_env_from_tf.sh  # now picks up CONFLUENT_GLOBAL_KEY / _SECRET from IaC/rtce

The Lightning query is scoped by catalog_name = environment id (FLINK_ENV_ID) and database_name = Kafka cluster id (KAFKA_CLUSTER_ID). These are ids, not the display names the Flink SQL Statements API uses. Restart the backend so it reloads apps/backend/.env. The RTCE customer lookup then serves results.

docs.title: Optional modules
docs.text:
These need AWS credentials. Each wrapper refreshes the AWS SSO token if needed and exports temporary credentials for the profile in AWS_PROFILE (default default). tf_aws.sh and tf_ec2.sh also check that the profile resolves to the expected account (EXPECTED_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID; set it empty to skip).

# RDS PostgreSQL + Secrets Manager (needs CONFLUENT_CLOUD_API_KEY/SECRET exported)
./scripts/tf_aws.sh apply

# Managed Debezium CDC connector (needs IaC/ccloud and IaC/AWS applied first)
./scripts/tf_connector.sh apply

# App host (needs IaC/AWS applied first; copy terraform.tfvars.example first)
./scripts/tf_ec2.sh apply

For a local PostgreSQL and Debezium instead of these modules, see Local CDC.

docs.title: Web App and Backend Design
docs.text:
Version

Last updated: 2026-11-24

This note presents the backend design and implementation, as well as other tools to support the demonstration. It covers code maintenance and explains some integrations with Confluent Cloud Streamhouse capabilities.

docs.title: Requirements addressed
docs.text:
• Web App to present customers page and be able to add new customer, read the detail of one customer, update one, or delete one
  • Pages for accounts CRUD operations
  • Pages for transactions CR operations
  • Pages and backend to manage cards CRUD defined within an account
  • Local persistence with Postgresql database running in container
  • Change events published to Kafka by Debezium CDC running locally, or as managed confluent cloud connector.
  • TDD for backend and frontend
  • Run snapshot queries from UI to backend to Confluent cloud on top of fact tables
  • Execute lightning query from a backend and display result to Frontend
  • Chat interface to demonstrate querying business data using Real-time context engine.
  • Persist chat conversation into Kafka topics

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
The solution architecture looks like in the figure below:

The frontend is a classic single-page app over a REST backend.

The backend is organized in different layers to facilitate testing and enforce a clear separation of concerns. The structure mimics a microservice implementation, which means it will be straightforward to separate the customer, account, transactions, analytics, and chat modules into separate code repositories and package them as 12-factor applications.

docs.title: Frontend ↔ backend integration
docs.text:
The frontend (apps/frontend, React 19 + Vite + React Router) never calls fetch directly from a page. It is layered so the HTTP concern lives in one place:

  • src/config.ts — resolves the backend base URL once: VITE_API_BASE_URL ?? http://localhost:8000/api/v1.
  • src/api/client.ts — a thin request<T>() wrapper around fetch that sets JSON headers, unwraps 204 No Content, and turns non-2xx responses into a typed ApiError (reading FastAPI's { "detail": ... } body).
  • src/api/{customers,accounts,transactions,cards,analytics,dataProducts,chat,scenarios}.ts — one module per domain, exposing typed CRUD functions (listAccounts, getAccount, createAccount, …) that map 1:1 to the REST endpoints.
  • src/types/* — TypeScript interfaces mirroring the backend Pydantic models, so the request/response contract is checked at compile time.
  • src/pages/* and src/components/* — views call only the api/ functions; they never know the base URL or status-code handling.

On the backend side, main.py mounts every domain router under /api/v1 and enables CORS for the Vite dev origin (http://localhost:5173). The browser's VITE_API_BASE_URL and the backend's CORS allow-list are the two ends of the same contract.

docs.title: Backend design pattern (models · DAO · service · inventory)
docs.text:
Each domain — customers, accounts, cards, transactions, analytics, chat, data products, scenarios — is a similar vertical slice of small modules. Routing and HTTP stay thin; persistence and seeding are each isolated behind their own module:

Layer Module Responsibility API api/<domain>_resource.py FastAPI router. Validates input via the models, maps results/404/409 to HTTP. No business logic. Service <domain>/service.py Dispatch/orchestration. Delegates to the DAO. Postgres is the source of truth; Debezium publishes the changes to Kafka. Models <domain>/models.py Pydantic *Create / *Update / full models. The single schema contract shared by the API, the DAO, and (mirrored) the frontend types. DAO <domain>/db_sink.py Data-access object: the domain's PostgreSQL DDL, column list, row↔model mapping, and CRUD — built on the shared pool in db.py. Inventory <domain>/inventory.py CSV-backed seed store. Loads the committed seed CSV into typed models used to seed PostgreSQL.

Cross-cutting modules keep the slices DRY:

  • db.py — one lazily-created connection pool, a cursor() context manager (commit/rollback/return-to-pool), and reusable init_schema / seed_if_empty / CDC-publication helpers. Each db_sink supplies only its own DDL and mapping; the connection and transaction mechanics are written once here.
  • bootstrap.py — on startup (main.py lifespan), creates all tables + the c360_cdc_publication, then seeds customers → accounts → cards → transactions in FK order, each table only if empty (idempotent).
  • config.py — environment-derived Settings (DATABASE_URL, Kafka/SR credentials, topic names).

Who owns Kafka. Debezium (local container or the managed connector on RDS) is the only producer of the cdc.public.* topics; the backend has no Kafka producer for these entities.

A new domain is added by copying the slice, registering its router in main.py, and adding its init_db + seed_from_csv to bootstrap.py.

docs.text:
The database has four tables. The seeding order respects foreign-key dependencies: customers → accounts → cards → transactions.

  • Customers:

    customer_id     UUID            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    first_name      VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL,
    last_name       VARCHAR(100)    NOT NULL,
    email           VARCHAR(255)    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    phone           VARCHAR(30),
    date_of_birth   TIMESTAMPTZ,
    gender          VARCHAR(20),
    address         VARCHAR(500),
    city            VARCHAR(100),

    postal_code     VARCHAR(20),
    country         VARCHAR(60)     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'US',
    customer_since  TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    segment         VARCHAR(50),    -- e.g. 'RETAIL', 'SMB', 'ENTERPRISE'

    yearly_income   NUMERIC(18, 2),

)

  • Accounts: 

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    account_id      UUID            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    customer_id     UUID            NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    account_number  VARCHAR(20)     NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    account_type    VARCHAR(30)     NOT NULL,  -- 'CHECKING', 'SAVINGS', 'CREDIT', 'LOAN'
    currency        CHAR(3)         NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD',

)

  • Cards: 

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cards (
    card_id         UUID            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    account_id      UUID            NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    card_brand      VARCHAR(30)     NOT NULL,
    card_type       VARCHAR(20)     NOT NULL,
    card_number     VARCHAR(19)     NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    expires         DATE            NOT NULL,
    has_chip        BOOLEAN         NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    credit_limit    NUMERIC(18, 2),
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ     NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

)

  • Transactions: 

    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transactions (
    transaction_id   UUID           PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
    account_id       UUID           REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    customer_id      UUID           NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id),
    transaction_type VARCHAR(30)    NOT NULL,  -- 'DEBIT', 'CREDIT', 'TRANSFER', 'FEE', 'INTEREST'
    amount           NUMERIC(18, 2) NOT NULL,
    currency         CHAR(3)        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'USD',
    description      VARCHAR(500),
    merchant_name    VARCHAR(200),
    merchant_category VARCHAR(100),
    channel          VARCHAR(50),   -- 'ONLINE', 'ATM', 'POS', 'MOBILE', 'BRANCH'
    status           VARCHAR(20)    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'COMPLETED',
    transacted_at    TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    posted_at        TIMESTAMPTZ,
    created_at       TIMESTAMPTZ    NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    card_id          UUID           REFERENCES cards(card_id),
    use_chip         VARCHAR(30),
    merchant_city    VARCHAR(100),
    merchant_state   VARCHAR(50),
    zip              VARCHAR(10),
    CONSTRAINT transactions_account_or_card_chk

docs.title: Query Customer Profile Facts
docs.text: To query customer profiles directly from Kafka, there are multiple capabilities available. Using SQL as an interface and the Streamhouse architecture, it is possible to leverage a Flink snapshot query via the Confluent Cloud REST API for Flink statements, or use the Confluent Lightning Query via the Real-Time Context Engine.

docs.title: Analytics Dashboard — CRM Data Products
docs.text:
The C360 analytics dashboard (KPI tiles and distribution charts) does not pull every customer row and aggregate in the backend. The aggregates are materialized in Flink as a dedicated CRM analytic data product — five small tables built from fct_c360_profile:

Table Grain Feeds in the dashboard fct_crm_summary one global row (qscope='ALL') KPI totals, averages, data-quality rollup fct_crm_by_segment per customer segment segment counts + balance-by-segment fct_crm_by_generation per generation segment generation counts fct_crm_by_gender per gender gender counts fct_crm_by_country per country country counts (top-8 + "Other")

In live mode the backend (analytics/crm_provider.py) runs five trivial SELECT * snapshot queries — one per table — concurrently through the confluent-sql DB-API driver,

and analytics/crm_aggregate.py folds the pre-aggregated rows into the dashboard payload (DataAnalytics). Only the summary rows cross the wire; the aggregation stays in Flink.

docs.title: Real-Time Context Engine
docs.text:
This time the 'Assistant' user interface is to emulate an agent to call the Confluent real-time context engine to get real-time customer 360 profile data.

In a developer-centric demonstration, we would use a tool like Claude Code, Codex, or similar. Here we want to simulate a business user who wants to get business data directly from Kafka.

  • The frontend exposes a chat interface /pages/ChatPage.tsx with a sendChatMessage(text, history) javascript method to reach the backend via a HTTP POST to /chat

  • The backend resource api/chat_resource.py export an async function, which delegates to the service layer 

    @router.post("", response_model=ChatResponse, status_code=200)
async def post_chat(request: ChatRequest) -> ChatResponse:
  return await service.get_reply(request)

  • The service manages the support to stub mode to return canned text or live mode to run the Agno agent against the local LLM + RTCE context-engine MCP server.

  • Agno agent wires a local OpenAI-compatible LLM (an MLX server) to the Confluent Real-Time Context Engine context-engine MCP server. 
      model, server_params = _build_model_and_params()
  async with MCPTools(
      server_params=server_params,
      transport="streamable-http",
      timeout_seconds=_MCP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
  ) as tools:
      agent = Agent(model=model, tools=[tools], instructions=_INSTRUCTIONS, markdown=False)
      result = await agent.arun(input=prompt)
  return (result.content or "").strip()

The MCP server URL is derived from the Confluent (config.settings.rtce_mcp_url()). Auth is HTTP Basic with the org-wide GLOBAL key/secret. Agno SDK offers a set of constructs to simplify the definition of agent with prompt, tools, persistence...

It is interesting to note that an MCP ClientSession is stateful and single-session over streamable-HTTP. The implementation uses a session initiated from the frontend and maintained until the user resets it. The session_id is a cache key plus an Agno session ID. The frontend generates a UUID on the first submit, displays it, and sends it on every turn. A Reset button closes the server-side connection and starts a new UUID. Conversation continuity stays frontend-driven: the history is sent from the UI and injected into the prompt. The cache is purely for connection/agent reuse to reduce latency. The session_id also tags the Agno run for observability. The connection is lazily created on the first message of a session (preserving graceful degradation) and reused until reset. The idle TTL is set to 30 minutes, and a max-sessions cap evicts stale ones; app shutdown closes all. A per-session lock serializes a session's turns with support for reconnect-on-failure.

docs.title: Get Data Product Lineage and Metrics
docs.text:
The last part of the demonstration is to present a Flink-focused lineage with a data product view.

  • The frontend uses a DataProductsPage and StatementGraphPage

  • The backend exposes a REST resource in api/data_product_resource.py backed by data_products/service.py, data_products/providers.py, and data_products/confluent_client.py, following the same vertical-slice pattern.
  • The list of data products comes from JSON descriptor files in data_products/descriptors/; each graph is a static definition built from the dbt pipelines.

  • To build those JSON manifests there is a tool, build_descriptors, which offers a CLI to read dbt manifest.json and create the expected files for the backend: 

    cd pipelines
uv run python ../scripts/build_descriptors.py

  • To get live metrics the backend calls the Confluent Cloud REST API via data_products/confluent_client.py; the metrics query differs depending on whether the table_type is "streaming_table" or "materialized_table".

docs.title: Complex Event Processing Scenarios
docs.text:
The backend has a dedicated scenarios domain (scenarios/registry.py, scenarios/runner.py, scenarios/service.py) that drives the CEP demonstration. It exposes pre-scripted transaction sequences via api/scenario_resource.py. The frontend CEPPage lists all registered scenarios, lets the user select one, and triggers it; the backend injects the transactions into PostgreSQL so Debezium propagates them to Kafka where the Flink MATCH_RECOGNIZE queries fire.

Three scenarios are currently registered:

Scenario ID Label Pattern (Flink table) Description fraud-probe Fraud Probe fct_fraud_probe Micro-charge followed by two large charges on the same card — classic card-cloning pattern merchant-streak Merchant Streak fct_merchant_streak Three consecutive transactions in the same merchant category — loyalty signal smb-spike SMB Spike fct_smb_spike Three large business charges followed by a reversal — anomalous expense spike

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: Both tiers are tested independently, and the test layout mirrors the module layout above — one test file per layer per domain.

docs.title: Backend (apps/backend/tests, pytest)
docs.text:
Configured in pyproject.toml (testpaths = ["tests"], pythonpath = ["."]). Fixtures live in tests/conftest.py. The suite is split so most of it runs with no infrastructure:

  • Unit / isolated — the bulk of the suite. Exercises each layer at its boundary with the dependency mocked:
  • test_*_models.py — Pydantic validation and defaults on the model contract.
  • test_*_inventory.py / test_*_seed.py — CSV load, row↔model mapping, and idempotent seeding.
  • test_*_api.py, test_cors.py — router behavior via FastAPI TestClient (status codes, 404/409 mapping, CORS headers), with the DAO stubbed.
  • test_scenarios_*.py — scenario registry, runner logic, and service, all stubbed against the DB.
  • test_chat_*.py — agent, service, and conversation producer unit tests.
  • test_data_products_*.py — descriptor builder, descriptor parsing, and live-metric queries.
  • test_crm_*.py — CRM aggregate folding and snapshot provider.
  • Postgres integration — test_*_postgres.py. These require a live database and are auto-skipped when DATABASE_URL is unset (via the skip_without_postgres fixture / requires_postgres marker).

Seed isolation: the session-scoped isolate_seed_csvs fixture copies the committed seed CSVs to a temp dir and points *_CSV_PATH at the copies, so tests never mutate the checked-in seed files.

cd apps/backend
uv run pytest                 # unit suite (postgres tests skip without DATABASE_URL)
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://dbadmin:localdevonly@localhost:5432/c360db \
  uv run pytest               # include the postgres integration tests

docs.text:

  • src/pages/*.test.tsx, src/components/*.test.tsx — page and component rendering, routing, form submission, and the confirm/delete flows, with the api/ modules mocked.
